text: VN-Index likely to rebound and retest 1,700 points this week

HÀ NỘI - The stock market recorded a sharp decline last week, with widespread selling pushing the VN-Index below the 1,700-point threshold, while subdued liquidity and heavy foreign net selling weighed on investor sentiment.
The VN-Index, representing the Hochiminh Stock Exchange (HoSE), fell 2.66 per cent over the week to close at 1,688.79 points.
On the Hanoi Stock Exchange (HNX), the HNX-Index also suffered a steep decline, losing nearly 8 per cent, to finish at 234.59 points.
Trading activity on the HoSE remained subdued.
Average matched trading volume reached more than 664.7 million shares per session, slightly below the previous week's average.
However, average daily trading value edged up slightly to over VNĐ15 trillion (US$582 million).
On the HNX, trading activity weakened more noticeably.
Average daily volume fell 19.2 per cent week on week to 49.2 million shares, while average trading value dropped 21.75 per cent to VNĐ625.3 billion.
Foreign investors continued to exert significant pressure on the market.
They recorded combined net sales of nearly VNĐ3.4 trillion on the two exchanges during the week, including approximately VNĐ3.3 trillion on HoSE and VNĐ93.8 billion on HNX.
This week, developments in international markets are expected to remain an important factor influencing investor sentiment, particularly following a sharp sell-off in AI and technology stocks.
A key question is whether the latest correction reflects a valuation adjustment or signals the beginning of capital outflows from one of the major investment themes of recent years.
The market debut of AI company Anthropic was another development attracting attention.

The company priced its initial public offering at $83 per share and began trading on the Nasdaq under the ticker ANT on November 19. However, its shares fell in the November 20 session, while the Nasdaq continued to decline.
Nguyễn Duy Anh, investment portfolio management director at VCBF, said the potential reallocation of international capital following the technology sell-off was a factor worth monitoring.
Markets with more attractive valuations could attract renewed investor interest if global funds reduce their concentration in AI-related assets.
Domestically, the 1,700-point level is a key threshold for the VN-Index.

Nguyễn Đức Anh said the recovery after the benchmark touched 1,670 points could lead to a retest of 1,700 points, which it had recently fallen below, but this would not yet constitute a confirmed trend reversal.
An expert from Pinetree Securities said the short-term outlook should only be reassessed if the VN-Index closes above 1,700 points and trading liquidity exceeds its 20-session average.
Conversely, a close below 1,670 points would invalidate the short-term recovery scenario.
Analysts from Saigon - Hanoi Securities said the 1,650-1,680-point range was relatively reasonable, with short-term capital flows showing signs of improvement at lower price levels.
However, they noted that overall market quality had not improved significantly, as most sectors remained in downtrends or prolonged consolidation.
The VN-Index's short-term trend would become more clearly positive only if it moved above the 1,700-1,720-point range.
Meanwhile, an expert from Kirin Securities (CSI) expected the benchmark to stage a rebound and retest 1,700 points.
However, with capital flows remaining relatively weak, CSI continued to favour a wait-and-see approach and advised limiting new buying positions.
The possibility of a rebound towards 1,700 points has been highlighted by several market participants.

However, the benchmark's ability to reclaim the recently lost levels, an improvement in liquidity and easing foreign selling pressure remain important indicators for assessing whether the market is establishing a new balance or merely pausing after a sharp decline. - BIZHUB/VNS
